tagline: Lake roads where a church moved uphill ahead of the water.
intro: From Deersville the byway winds about 55 miles through Tappan Lake country and around Clendening Lake, with US 250 following Tappan Lake for several miles on causeways built along with the lake. A northern loop on SR 646 goes by Scio, Jewett and New Rumley. Delaware and Wyandot people traveled this country, and Moravians settled it.
There are towns under the water. The community of Tappan, which gave the lake its name, was flooded when the lake was finished, and so was Laceyville.

moments.title: Tappan Dam
moments.text: Eslick Road runs along the top of the dam, a vantage point over Tappan Lake.

moments.title: Pleasant Valley Church
moments.text: When the valley was flooded for Tappan Dam, the church and the graves in its cemetery were moved up this hill, and now they overlook the lake and US 250.

moments.title: New Rumley
moments.text: George Armstrong Custer was born here, and of the house only the foundations remain, beside Erwin Frey's statue of him along SR 646.
